first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in seychelles' because it's on our list next to Mauritius and I want to know if the legal side holds up. The intro answers that, names the Civil Status office and links the government pages so I can check them myself. No turquoise-water waffle. Went to the FAQ first like always. The timing answer is solid: 11 days of banns, or a special licence normally issued within two days. But the beach question gets a muddled non-answer, witnesses is 'ask the office', and every government fee on the page (special licence, officer's fee) is 'a fee applies' with no figure. Wedded Wonderland stays out of the way until near the end, which I respect, but nothing tells me what they cost or whether they take a cut from the resort.

journey.quote: The Seychelles is on your shortlist, and before you choose a bay or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Straight answer to the question I came with. Good start.
Intro says flatly 'It will.' FAQ says 'in most cases'. The hedge is the honest one, so the intro should match it. Small, but it's the kind of gap I notice when someone's selling to me.

journey.quote: The banns run for eleven days before the wedding, and a special marriage licence, normally issued within two days, can shorten that wait.
journey.reaction: Actual numbers I can book flights and leave around. This is the answer I wanted.

journey.quote: Registration is made in the office, and couples who wish to register their marriage at home tell the Civil Status office at least a week before.
journey.reaction: I asked 'can we marry on the beach' and got this. So is it the office or not? What does 'at home' mean when we live in Brisbane? Then it tells me to ask the office and the resort. A yes, no or 'not published' would be better than this.

journey.quote: Ask the Civil Status office when you contact it.
journey.reaction: Witnesses is a yes/no question and the answer is homework. The body text at least admits it isn't on the official list. Say that here too.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in the Seychelles?
journey.quote: Read it together once, before you sign anything with a resort.
journey.reaction: Advice that protects me before money changes hands. A pure sales page wouldn't say that.

journey.quote: The Australian High Commission's guidance for couples marrying in the Seychelles is that a church wedding without a civil ceremony is not legally recognised, so the civil marriage comes first.
journey.reaction: That's a catch, stated and sourced. Exactly what I'm after.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Australia has no embassy, high commission or consulate in the Seychelles.
journey.reaction: Honest about a real downside, plus the passport point. Most destination pages would bury this.

journey.section: What the Civil Status office asks for
journey.quote: One question to settle early: whether the office accepts certified copies of your birth and divorce certificates, or wants the originals.
journey.reaction: Fair to flag it rather than guess. Adds to the 'ask the office' list though.

journey.section: The banns and a special licence
journey.quote: It is normally issued within two days of the application, and a fee applies.
journey.reaction: How much? It's a government fee, it should be public. It goes in my spreadsheet either way. Give me the figure with a date or link straight to where it's published.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies when both of you are foreigners.
journey.reaction: Second unquantified fee, and a 'higher rate' on other islands plus the officer's transport, accommodation and meals. Good that the extras are named, but with no numbers I can't compare an outer island against Mahé.

journey.quote: Witnesses do not appear on the document list for two foreigners.
journey.reaction: Honest about what the source does and doesn't say. I'd rather this than a made-up number.

journey.quote: Plan a weekday morning for it in the days after the wedding, and keep the original safe in your hand luggage on the way home.
journey.reaction: Supreme Court apostille plus a Ministry letter in one weekday morning? How long do those actually take? That decides our flight home.

journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the friends who could not make the flight.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' based on what? Harmless, but it's an unsupported claim on a page that sources everything else.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: If a resort presents a wedding package, ask whether it covers the civil formalities, the officer's attendance and the certificate errands after the wedding, and ask for that list in writing.
journey.reaction: That's my question to every vendor. The deposits question above it is the other one I'd ask. A planner telling me to grill the resort is a good sign.

journey.section: When to marry in the Seychelles
journey.quote: Many beaches have strong currents and rips, with few lifeguards or warning signs, and conditions change with the season.
journey.reaction: Monsoon, dengue, rips: the downsides are all here with sources. That's how you earn trust with me.

journey.quote: If you would like to weigh the islands against your guest list, talk it through with Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: First sales nudge. It comes after the evidence and it's one line, so I can live with it.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Inclusions in writing is the right promise. 'Plans your payments' is where I ask whether they take a cut from the resort. Nothing here says, and there's no real Seychelles wedding to back it up.

journey.section: Plan your Seychelles wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it, from the island you choose to the hour you marry, is where the planning starts.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the friends who could not make the flight.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported 'many couples' generalisation on a page that otherwise backs every claim with a source.

turn_offs_found.quote: Registration is made in the office, and couples who wish to register their marriage at home tell the Civil Status office at least a week before.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ heading asks whether we can marry on the beach and the answer dodges it. It reads like an answer but leaves me unsure whether a beach ceremony can be the legal one.

turn_offs_found.quote: It is normally issued within two days of the application, and a fee applies.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions a cost with no figure or link. Same for the officer's fee. For someone building a budget spreadsheet, an unquantified fee looks like the catch.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the 11-day banns and two-day special licence, plus the document list, for our planning spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread: the resort question list (deposits, officer's attendance, package inclusions in writing) and the warning that a church wedding alone isn't legally recognised

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and the promises are concrete: AUD quotes, fee agreed in writing. But my real questions, how the fee is worked out and whether they take a cut from Seychelles resorts, aren't answered. The guide gets them a look at their site, not a call yet. I'd email those questions before committing to anything.

top_3_changes: Beach FAQ: answer the question in the heading. If the source pack confirms the officer can register a marriage away from the office, say so plainly first; if it doesn't, say openly that the office's published guidance doesn't spell this out, then give the 'one week's notice' rule. Clarify what registering 'at home' means for couples who live overseas, or drop the phrase if the source doesn't explain it.

Government fees: where the page says 'a fee applies' (special licence, officer's fee), give the current amount with a source and date (flagged for checking), or say the Civil Status office sets the fee and link the exact page beside the sentence.

Tidy the loose bits: make the intro's 'It will.' match the FAQ's 'In most cases, yes.' hedge, change 'Many couples do exactly that' to something that doesn't claim a number (e.g. 'Some couples follow it with a long lunch at home'), and in the witnesses FAQ say plainly that the official document list doesn't mention witnesses before telling us to ask.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for the catch and the numbers, flagged unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers and paperwork help listed as deferred unanswered questions, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Top changes require no new business facts; any government fee figure or beach-ceremony rule must come from a source

open_questions.question: Does the source pack confirm whether the Civil Status Officer can register a marriage at a resort or beach (fact_206 implies travel to other islands, fact_203 says registration is in the office), and does it hold the special licence or officer fee amounts? If yes, the beach confusion and fee objections close with sourced lines; if not, an explicit 'not published' line plus a direct link is the fallback.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'getting married in seychelles' while the Seychelles is on the shortlist and he is comparing planners; relevance is 4 because the legal content is what he wanted, and enquiry likelihood is 2 because his fee and commission questions about Wedded Wonderland stay open.
Business details (fees, commissions, ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deferred by the brief; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Rendered link text was quoted without markdown link syntax, as a reader would see it.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, legal and document sections, ceremony and certificate sections, the resort question list and the Wedded Wonderland sections, with a skim of the entry, climate and island sections.
